Its agents analyze robot data and surface the patterns that matter, so engineers spend less time digging through the last run and more time building the next. Investment has also come from leaders and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter and Carbon Robotics, along with several of Alloy's customers.

hits.title: Alloy Robotics Raises $8M in New Funding to Help Engineers Debug Robot Fleets With AI Agents
hits.snippet: - Alloy Robotics raised $8 million at an $80 million valuation to expand its AI-agent platform for diagnosing robot failures and improving fleet reliability. - Square Peg led the round, with participation from Blackbird, Airtree, Skip Capital and executives and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter and Carbon Robotics. - Alloy said its platform supports nearly 1,000 robots and has analyzed more than 10,000 missions, combining logs, telemetry, video and engineering context while also connecting with coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code through Model Context Protocol. ... Leading the funding round was Square Peg with participation from existing investors Blackbird, Airtree and Skip Capital, according to Alloy. The financing also included executives and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter and Carbon Robotics.
